subtopics.title: Reading a Formula Like a Sentence

questions.question: In cost = R450 + R12,50 × km, the R450 represents:
options: The fixed charge, owed regardless of distance

questions.question: The R12,50 in the formula is:
options: The rate — the amount each kilometre adds to the bill

questions.question: In this formula, cost is called the DEPENDENT variable because:
options: It appears on the right-hand side
The cost depends on the distance driven
The distance depends on the cost

subtopics.title: Forward Substitution — Pricing the 340 km Trip

questions.question: The cost of a 340 km trip is:
A learner computes (450 + 12,50) × 340 = R157 250. What went wrong?
options: Order of operations — multiplication must happen before addition

questions.question: Why should the formula and the substitution line be set out before calculating?
options: Each line typically earns its own mark and lets the marker follow your method
It is required by the calculator

questions.question: Which sense check confirms R4 700 is plausible for the 340 km trip?
options: The answer should be less than R450
The driving charge (R4 250) should far exceed the fixed fee (R450) on a long trip — and it does

subtopics.title: Reverse Substitution — How Far Does R1 200 Go?

questions.question: With a budget of R1 200, the first step after substituting is:
options: Subtract the R450 fixed charge from both sides, leaving R750 for driving

questions.question: R1 200 buys a trip of:
Dividing the whole R1 200 by R12,50 gives 96 km. Why is this wrong?
options: R450 of the budget pays the fixed fee and never buys kilometres — it must be removed first

questions.question: How is the answer of 60 km verified?
options: Substitute forwards: 450 + 12,50 × 60 = R1 200, exactly the budget

subtopics.title: The General Method, the Classic Traps, and Where This Skill Lives

questions.question: The correct unwinding order for reverse substitution in a fixed-plus-rate formula is:
options: Divide by the rate first, then subtract the fixed part
Multiply by the rate, then add the fixed part
Subtract the fixed part first, then divide by the rate
Any order gives the same answer

questions.question: A formula requires kilometres but the question gives 4 500 metres. You should:
When should rounding happen in a multi-step substitution?
options: Only at the final answer — carry full values through the working

subtopics.title: The Gate Fee and the Meter

questions.question: In the soccer-match comparison, the R450 hire charge plays the part of:
options: The gate fee paid once at the entrance

questions.question: Which clue in the formula tells you R12,50 is the repeating charge?
options: It is multiplied by the kilometres, so it is charged once for every kilometre
It comes second in the formula

questions.question: Which everyday bill has the SAME skeleton as this formula?
options: A plumber's call-out fee plus an hourly rate

questions.question: Why are the kilometres called the independent variable?
options: They are always the bigger number
You choose them freely, and the cost answers back

subtopics.title: Running the Machine Forwards — and the R157 250 Disaster

questions.question: 340 kilometres at R12,50 each comes to:
In plain words, what does adding R450 to R12,50 BEFORE multiplying actually do?
options: It gives a small rounding error
It charges the R450 gate fee once for every one of the 340 kilometres

questions.question: 340 × R450 = R153 000. What is this amount in the wrong answer of R157 250?
options: The phantom gate fees that were never charged

questions.question: What makes R4 700 a believable hire-car bill?
options: Most of it is driving (R4 250) with a small admin charge on top

subtopics.title: Running It Backwards — R1 200 in Your Pocket

questions.question: Out of a R1 200 budget, how much can actually turn into kilometres?
The wrong answer of 96 km is exactly 36 km too far. Where do those 36 km come from?
options: R450 divided by R12,50 — the fixed fee spent as if it bought driving

questions.question: Why is 'shoes off before socks' a good picture for reverse substitution?
options: You undo the steps in the opposite order from how they were done
It reminds you to slow down

questions.question: Running 60 km back through the formula gives 450 + 12,50 × 60 = R1 200. This shows that:
options: The answer lands exactly on the budget given, so it is proven correct
